html:
Saint-Domingue, the French western third of Hispaniola, became in the 1700s the richest colony in the world. It grew a large share of the sugar and coffee that Europe consumed.

French buccaneers and settlers had moved into the west after Spain emptied it in the Devastations of Osorio, and Spain recognised French rule in 1697. Planters then imported Africans on a vast scale through the Atlantic slave trade. By the 1780s close to half a million enslaved people lived there, far outnumbering whites and free people of colour.

Death rates on the sugar estates were so high that the colony depended on constant new arrivals. Its wealth and cruelty came to an end with the Haitian Revolution of 1791.
sum: Saint-Domingue, the French western third of Hispaniola, became in the 1700s the richest colony in the world. It grew a large share of the sugar and coffee that Europe consumed.
